study_material.title: Algebra - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: Placement algebra covers linear and quadratic equations, algebraic identities, polynomials and simple inequalities. The identities (a+b)^2, a^2-b^2, a^3+b^3 and the sum/product of quadratic roots do most of the heavy lifting.
learning_objectives: Use sum and product of roots without solving
Apply standard identities including x + 1/x forms
Handle simple inequalities and the remainder theorem

concepts.heading: 1. Linear Equations
concepts.body: Isolate the variable step by step. Two-variable systems: eliminate one variable by adding/subtracting scaled equations, or substitute. x + y = 10 and x - y = 4 give x = 7, y = 3 by adding then halving.

concepts.heading: 2. Quadratic Equations
concepts.body: ax^2 + bx + c = 0 solves by factoring, completing the square, or x = (-b +- sqrt(b^2-4ac))/2a. Discriminant D = b^2 - 4ac: D > 0 two real roots, D = 0 equal roots, D < 0 no real roots.

concepts.heading: 3. Sum and Product of Roots
concepts.body: For ax^2 + bx + c = 0: sum of roots = -b/a, product = c/a. Many questions need only these - never solve if sum/product suffice. x^2 - 7x + 10 = 0 has sum 7, product 10 (roots 2 and 5).

concepts.heading: 5. Remainder Theorem and Inequalities
concepts.body: Dividing polynomial f(x) by (x - a) leaves remainder f(a). For inequalities, flip the sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative number; otherwise solve like equations.

shortcut_methods: Check options by substitution when equations look messy
Use sum/product of roots to skip the quadratic formula
a^2 - b^2 factors instantly - look for difference of squares
common_mistakes: Sign errors when moving terms across the equals sign
Forgetting to flip inequality signs with negative multipliers
Using c/a for sum of roots instead of -b/a
study_material.summary: Identities plus sum/product of roots solve most questions without grinding; keep signs disciplined and the chapter is safe marks.
